      HOW TO WRITE TO OUTLET
      ----------------------
Letters are accepted  in  almost
any form for publication in our
OUTLETTERS: BASIC PRINT or  DATA
statements, handwritten or typed
pages, a simple  JOTTER  program
is provided in Issue 2(Opus #4);
mailbox messages via Prestel No.
014703943 but the easiest for us
to edit are Tasword 2 files with
the right-hand margin set at 32.

Please state if there should  be
parts of your letter you do  not
wish published but we always use
our discretion  anyway.  Letters
may also be edited  for  clarity
and length... Please ask if  you
welcome  direct   correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From: Spiros Gaoutsis, Salisbury

Dear Ron,

Thank you for the issues of
OUTLET 5 & 6 which I received
yesterday but also I would like
to thank you for your compliment
about my English. My wife thinks
that my English are teribble,
especialy the speling. Anyway,
the point of writing this letter
is that I can't get enough of
OUTLET and so I am enclosing a
P/O for Issues 5 & 6.[B carts]

Thank you for publishing my
letter and the advert but for
the advert I forgot to place the
price of `35.00 for both [See
OUTBOARD - BC]

In one of ZX COMPUTING issues I
read a review of BONABANNER but
I would like to know a little
bit more about it please if
possible.

Ron, here I am afraid I will
have to ask you if it is
possible to transfer OUTLET
issues to tape for storage
because I will run out of
cartridges soon and the only way
for me to get them will be by
mail order only. I used to buy
my cartridges in BOOTS but they
do not sell computer hardware
any more. I went this morning
for some cartridges but they do
not sell 'em any more although
they are selling SPECDRUMS for
`12.99 a kit.

If you want to tell to other
OUTLET readers: Woolworths are
selling packs of 5 games:AUF
WIEDERSEHEN MONTY, MASK, DEATH
WISH 3, JACK THE NIPPER II and
THING BOUNCES BACK for `9.99. I
am not into games but I got a
pack just to have around.

I am sorry for taking so much of
your valuable time and before
you say it I know I am a pain in
the !*#%@'!

        Yours sincerely,

          Spiros Gaoutsis

P.S. Next time I go back home to
Greece I will send you a post
card.

To: Spiros Gaoutsis from Brian

"Not into games"!- Cor! Leave it
out Spiros!- Bet the games pack
is in and out of your cassette
player like a ferret in a drain
pipe factory.

Information about our BONABANNER
program can be found in BONADEMO
in this issue on Cartridge B.

We're looking into the problem
of cassette back-up for OUTLET
but don't hold your breath (Well
you can if you want).The problem
is finding the time to develop
the software.It could take weeks
of effort with no guarantee of
success. The most positive thing
that anyone wanting a tape back-

up routine can do is contribute
something else to OUTLET - A
small program or even a picture.
I'm sure readers would be
interested in anything created
with ARTIST II, ART STUDIO, etc.
How about a title page for
OUTLET? (If you show the Issue
number and month make sure you
do it AT LEAST 3 MONTHS AHEAD!).

We need articles. We're not too
bothered about spelling and
grammar. We can polish that up
when we edit it. Next time you
are writing about a particular
subject in a letter to us just
keep going for a few paragraphs.
Before you know where you are
you'll have half a page (2 or 3
Spectrum screens)on one subject.

Then, if you dry up, come back
to it later and add to it. You
only need one A4 page or so (4
or 5 Spectrum screens)for a very
short article. Many letters we
receive are longer than that but
they obviously cover different
subjects. Stick to one theme and
HEY PRESTO!- you've an article
not a letter! If you can expand
on it so much the better.Ideally
it would be in a Tasword 2 file,
with the right margin set at 32
but we accept hand-written or
printed pages, JOTTER files etc.

You see, the best thing anyone
can do to support OUTLET and to
raise the quality is to send in
something.That frees us to spend
more time developing better and

more sophisticated software for
OUTLET. Don't underestimate the
importance of even a single item
contributed to OUTLET - it can
save us hours of work which can
then be applied elsewhere.

                   - Brian

From: John White
To: Ron & Brian

First, to close [what, already?]
the subject of my faulty RAM
chip I have now replaced it with
a 4164 [plus a socket!] and my
Spectrum is behaving perfectly.
By re-editing my Tasword files I
have increased the spare disc
space from 75K to 120K, as files
are now saved with their proper
length instead of at least 204
lines [see my letters in recent
OUTLETs]. I am very grateful for
all the helpful suggestions I
have received. Second,here is my
entry for the February JIG!BLOX
Competition.    Best wishes
             from John White.

     Thanks, John. - Brian

From Steve Monk - Ashford

Dear Ron & Brian

Firstly may I offer some help to
Tom Ashmore who in the last
issue was inquiring about
CATologue's and knowing what
files where what and at what
addresses they where.

Well maybe he should get a copy
of The Spectrum Shadow ROM
Disassembly. It's published by
Melbourne House and in it are
some very useful routines
including a *CAT,n which gives
you a list of programs on
drive,n as they are found also
the file type, code address and
the line start number if it is a
basic program .

I have found it very useful to
see where you chaps at OUTLET
have put your code when I hack
into some of your programs to
tailor them for my purposes .

I too can endorse Stephen Lamb
in saying that there are some
good articles in Everyday
Electronics magazine .

Since I have had a lot of time
off work just lately due to a
back injury I have built an
analogue to digital converter
and also several other micro
controlled projects for my
Speccy, all with some ideas from
this mag and also a good book
called Spectrum Interfacing and
projects by Graham Bishop.

I hope to control a train layout
using my now redundant spectrum+
(due to the purchase of +2) it's
well within the means of it. As
they say somewhere on telly 'WE
HAVE THE TECHNOLOGY ' or VORT
SPRUNG SPRIKKY DICK or words to
that effect. Bye for now: Steve.

Thanks, Steve. I've asked Ron to
look at his copy of the book you
mentioned - I don't recollect
seeing that *CAT. I wonder if it
is the same as the *CAT that was
given away with expansion packs?
Our local Smiths don't seem to
stock Everyday Electronics but I
will keep looking. Sorry to hear
you've had back trouble - hope
you get over that quickly.-BRIAN

From: Norman Pritchard, Newport

Dear Ron & Brian,
Am returning February A+B as I
have difficulty loading, etc...
[Now replaced - BC] ...By what I
have managed to see so far, this
month's OUTLET looks better than
ever so keep up the good work.

One suggestion, if I may be so
bold. Some parts of the programs
talk about "dumps" and "go to"
etc. which are items familiar to
all you "Clive Sinclairs" but
there are some of us out here
who could do with a little
explanation sometimes. So come
on you two - spare a thought for
us "Thickies".
              Very best wishes,
              Norman Pritchard.

To Norman Pritchard From Brian

Trust you now have the replace-
ment Issue 6 and all is well.Ron
is using a new FORMAT routine so
we hope that there will be less
load failures in future.

I take your point about not
assuming that everyone knows the
terms that we take for granted.
It would be impractical and
boring to those who DO know the
common terminology to give a
detailed explanation every time
an expression comes up and, of
course, we are getting new
readers all the time. The answer
may be to set up some definitive
explanations in OUTCLASS and
refer people to that.I expect to
introduce this shortly. - Brian

From: Paul Rosenthal, Worcs.

Dear Ron & Brian,

Thanks for sending Issue No.5 of
OUTLET through so quickly and I
must say that it's great to find
other people who use their
Spectrums for things other than
games playing.

I personally love anything to do
with machine code and getting to
grips with writing programs
using it, but I'm afraid I have
not produced any masterpieces as
yet. (The time to attempt it
would be nice!!). I like the new
twin cartridge format, twice the
entertainment I suppose and was
quite amused by the serial. I
particularly enjoyed switching

on the light in the cellar and
was impressed by the full screen
horizons. Can they continue to
keep surpassing themselves I
say?

The "LPROMPT" program was very
good and I'm intrigued by the
fact that the Spectrum Manual
lists the system variable as
"not used". I would be
interested to hear more about
the facts behind it. I'm afraid
that I tried out the error
trapping routine whilst
attempting to load "OUTBOARD".
Works very well it does, which
is more than can be said for
"OUTBOARD" on my particular
cartridge. Still it'll take more
than that to dampen my
enthusiasm for your creativity.

Keep up the good work and when
will you be at the ZX Microfair
again?
         Paul Rosenthal
Thanks Paul.Glad you're enjoying
"TICKET!".Don't hesitate to send
in any program you've done- It
doesn't have to be a masterpiece
and we can always give it a
facelift if needed. I don't know
why those system variables are
unused. They must have been put
in at the early planning stage
of the ROM and then not needed.
I believe Ron has now replaced
the faulty cartridge? Sorry! -
we have no plans at the moment
to go to another ZXM.We are both
utterly stretched during this
period. We cannot spare the 2 to
3 days it would need to arrange
and attend. Wish we could.-Brian

From: Ian Vaudrey, London, SW9

Dear Mr. Cavers,

Thank you for the copy of OUTLET
#7, received a few days ago. In
it I noticed a letter from B.
McLellan, in which he asks if
anyone knows how to transfer
"TRIVIAL PURSUIT" to microdrive.
Well, I know how to transfer it
to the Discovery and I think
that the same method will work
for Microdrive.

If you've seen the SDC [SPECTRUM
DISCOVERY CLUB,see OUTBOARD.-BC]
Newsletter then you may know
that, since Issue 3, I've had a
regular slot covering tape to
disk transfer of games software
wthout the use of a "magic

button" interface or any
utilities.I also answer members'
queries on this subject and
enclosed is a listing of a
program I knocked up in reply to
a member's letter...  [details]

...I hope this is of some use.
Please let me know if you would
be interested in this sort of
program for inclusion in future
issues of OUTLET. I could, of
course, supply runnable programs
on disk if so.

Finally, is there any charge for
the inclusion of an item in
OUTBOARD and in what form should
the item be submitted?
                    Best Wishes,
                    Ian Vaudrey

To: Ian Vaudrey from Brian

Many thanks, Ian. Ron has passed
on a copy of your listing to Mr.
McLellan. If anyone else would
like a copy let us know. We'd be
glad of any further help of this
sort which is absolutely crucial
for anyone without a Multiface-
type device. I suppose the wise
course is to invite readers to
write in with any tape to drive
transfer problems and see if you
have the answer which we'll
include in OUTLET if you supply
it on disc (We'll put it on the
microdrive and Disciple version
too of course!).

No charge for OUTBOARD and any
form will do (JOTTER or DATA is
easiest for us)    - Brian

From W. Frank Harris,  Hexham

Dear Brian,

After the last seven issues, I
still like OUTLET. Mainly, it's
the novelty: nothing else comes
through my mailbox and talks
about commonplace computer-
things through my Spectrum and
its 3 x MD battery. For my vote,
you can drop the competitions,
puzzles and games - I use the
computer almost wholly for
Tasword Three letter-writing
(including Open University
assignments), home accounting
and computational work. For the
latter,I'd like better programm-
ing skill but, time being short,
stick to (long-winded) BASIC.

Utilities to make programs
easier to write (rather than
fancy lettering programs) would
be welcome - e.g. an easy-to-use
graphing program for scientific
formulae. So would programs,
utilities, tips, routines etc.
with a practical end-use other
than pretty pictures. The
exception to prove this rule was
your "large letter" program
which was very effective when I
used the screen as a visual aid
in a local talk.

My printer is a Brother HR10 via
Kempston E: but your programs
seldom work on it - I always
have to command COPY: REM/1
before line-feed works- or amend
the program. A disconcertingly

high percentage of programs fail
to load. Could be the fault of
my equipment I suppose - I
sometimes "lose" my own files-
even whole carts with the "MD
not present" disagnosis. Is it
really not possible to fish out
byte-by-byte content from these
format-aborted carts?

The letters you publish are
often repetitious - a little
more ruthlessness is suggested
to cut out the banal. Your
subscribers' points of import
can benefit from conciseness.
You may wish to consider
presenting two types of letter
separately - the "computer"
letter for Speccy buffs) and
"wider view" letter (e.g. about

OUTLET). Letters which wallow on
from one subject to the next
(like this one) become wearying.

Finally, keep listening to your
subscribers - but keep making
your own decisions about OUTLET.
It's an innovative product - but
will need updating and freshen-
ing before your subscribers lose
interest. Keep it meaty and
packed with sound, interesting
Sp+MD matter and we'll put up
with quite a bit that only the
other nut finds interesting.Long
may it continue to be a welcome
monthly visitor - even when, as
is inevitable, the novelty wears
off. Good luck.

            W. Frank Harris

To Frank Harris from Brian

Some good points there, Frank.
Sorry about the printer problem
but if we put a COPY:REM/1 in
our routines it may spoil the
print-outs of everyone else who
is using the Kempston E. The
solution may be to alter the
dipswitch setting on your
printer. Check your printer
manual for dipswitch line feed
settings Meanwhile, can any
other Kempston E user say
whether they have this problem?

Despite all we do, there seems
to be an inevitable percentage
of microdrive load failures but
don't hesitate to return such
cartridges and we'll replace


them promptly. As for your own
files - It's possible to buy
byte editors that can recover
some lost files but the process
is so difficult, time- consuming
and downright dubious that I was
thinking of making a competition
out of one! However, these byte-
editors are of little use on
cartridges that merely return
"microdrive not present".

I am now cutting letters more
and more - mainly because I
think the size of OUTLETTERS has
reached saturation point
relative to the overall size of
the magazine - and obviously I
will snip away the dross before
the substance but I hope we keep
this informal "chat" atmosphere
going.

A simple, two-dimensional graph
program might be feasible.
If you can reduce a formula to
two coordinates, e.g. time and
growth, I think I could produce
a program to which one could
input data - even over a long
period with a SAVE option - that
would display the information in
graph form, bar or pie chart. In
fact with 2 or 3 sets of data
superimposed for comparison. If
you've a particular application
in mind I'd be interested if you
could let me have something to
work at and I'll see what I can
do.
              - Brian

From: John Taylor, Grantham

Dear Ron & Brian,
      ....One idea you might get
someone to work on for you is to
do a complete index of all the
OUTLET cartridges so far. This
would be ideal on say MASTERFILE
with a short descripton of each
program or routine.As my library
of OUTLET grows so managing it
becomes more of a necessity....
   Bye for now and God Bless,
           John Taylor
Thanks, John. I'm keeping your
MISTERMIND strategy to myself
for now! Let 'em suffer I say!
Ron is working on a back issues
file but it will be in issue
order. I think you may be right
about an index though - I'll put
another note in my tray! - Brian.

From: Jacques Singelee, Brussels

Dear Ron and Brian,

   Congratulations on your
excellent work and thank you for
Issues 5,6,7.

Suggestions: It seems you do not
have enough room on one disk to
put all you want on it. I find
that the interest of an issue on
disk is that we have screens and
programs that we can use later
in our own programs. Screens are
nearly impossible to transfer by
means of a paper issue, programs
are long to enter and errors are
current.So,in this way is a disk
based issue very interesting.

The published letters take
certainly half the room on a
disk and this valuable room
should be occupied with programs
and screens! It is also not very
[enjoyable]to read text screens!
So I suggest you make an issue
with letters,info and directions
for use, on paper and all the
rest on disk with a general
menu.

I regret that there is generally
no option to print the
directions for use of the
programs. (I don't find them
possibly!) I find the idea of a
disk for newcomers very, very,
good!

Waiting for next issue as soon
as possible!     - Jacques

To: Jacques Singelee from Brian

Mercie bien,Jacques.

We try to include options to
dump program instructions where
possible. Problems are:  1.With
a wide range of interfaces,print
routines use up extra memory,
especially if used in every
program.  2.It becomes very
difficult to highlight the text
on screen for presentation or
emphasis as the colour codes
cause problems if you send that
same text to the printer.  3.It
is often extremely difficult to
alter contributed programs once
written. 4.Some instructions
merely explain and contain no
real "data" that you need to


refer to again. You will note
that one solution we're using in
this issue is to put the
instructions into OUTLET
separately as a text file with
the full print options. Another,
as in HANDYWIDE last month,is to
have an option to dump a SUMMARY
of the instructions. Comment ca
va? Tres bien, oui?

OUTLETTERS actually takes up
about one sixth of the space of
the full OUTLET but the idea of
producing half of OUTLET as hard
copy does have its attractions
and is on our hit-list of
options.       - Brian

From Adrian Stocks, Richmond

Dear Ron & Brian,

OUTLET 6 included my letter that
mentioned in passing that an
EP44 typewriter of mine had been
lost while in for repair at W.H.
Smiths' It's only fair for me
now to point out that the matter
has been resolved and, thanks to
the work put in  by Smiths',
Messrs. Brother have supplied me
with a brand new machine to
replace the one they lost. A
happy ending! (at last).

          Adrian Stocks

Thanks, Adrian. You'll probably
be interested in the EP44toT2
program in this issue. - Brian.

     КАК НАПИСАТЬ В OUTLET
     ---------------------
Письма принимаются практически в
любом виде для публикации в
наших OUTLETTERS: операторы
PRINT или DATA в Бейсике,
рукописные или напечатанные на
машинке страницы; простая
программа JOTTER есть в Issue 2

От: Spiros Gaoutsis, Salisbury

Дорогой Ron,

Спасибо за выпуски OUTLET 5 и 6,
которые я получил вчера, а также
я хотел бы поблагодарить за
комплимент по поводу моего
английского. Моя жена считает,
что мой английский ужасен,
особенно правописанее. Как бы то
ни было, цель этого письма — мне
всё мало OUTLET, поэтому я
прилагаю почтовый перевод за
выпуски 5 и 6 [картриджи B].

Спасибо за публикацию моего
письма и объявления, но в
объявлении я забыл указать цену
в `35.00 за оба [см. OUTBOARD —
BC].

В одном из номеров ZX COMPUTING
я читал обзор BONABANNER, но мне
хотелось бы узнать о ней чуть
побольше, если возможно.

Ron, боюсь, мне придется спросить
вас, можно ли переносить выпуски
OUTLET на ленту для хранения,
потому что картриджи у меня скоро
закончатся, и единственный способ
их достать — заказывать по почте.
Раньше я покупал картриджи в

цене `12.99 за комплект.

продают сборники из 5 игр: AUF
WIEDERSEHEN MONTY, MASK, DEATH
WISH 3, JACK THE NIPPER II и
THING BOUNCES BACK за `9.99. Я
не особо играю, но взял пачку
просто чтобы была.

Извините, что отнял столько
вашего драгоценного времени, и
прежде чем вы это скажете, я сам
знаю, что я заноза в !*#%@'!

       Искренне ваш,

         Spiros Gaoutsis

P.S. В следующий раз, когда поеду
домой в Грецию, я пришлю вам
открытку.

Кому: Spiros Gaoutsis от Brian

«Не особо играю»! — Ну и ну!
Брось, Spiros! — Спорим, сборник
игр летает туда-сюда из твоего
магнитофона, как хорек по заводу
водосточных труб!

Информация о нашей программе
BONABANNER находится в BONADEMO в
этом номере на картридже B.

Мы изучаем вопрос создания копий
OUTLET на кассетах, но не
затаивайте дыхание (хотя, если
хотите, можете). Проблема в том,
чтобы найти время на разработку
софта. Это может потребовать
недель усилий без всякой
гарантии успеха. Самое полезное,
что может сделать каждый, кто
хочет подпрограмму сброса на
ленту, — прислать что-нибудь для
OUTLET. Небольшую программу или
даже картинку. Уверен, читателям
было бы интересно все, что
создано в ARTIST II, ART STUDIO
и т.д. Как насчет титульного
экрана для OUTLET? (Если будете
указывать номер выпуска и месяц,
убедитесь, что делаете это
МИНИМУМ НА 3 МЕСЯЦА ВПЕРЕД!).

Нам нужны статьи. Мы не особо
переживаем насчет орфографии и
грамматики. Мы можем все
причесать при редактуре. В
следующий раз, когда будете
писать на какую-то конкретную
тему в письме нам, просто
продолжайте еще пару абзацев. Не
успеете оглянуться, как у вас
выйдет полстраницы (2 или 3
экрана Спектрума) на одну тему.

Затем, если мысли иссякнут,
вернитесь к этому позже и
допишите. Для очень короткой
статьи нужна всего лишь одна
страница A4 (4 или 5 экранов
Спектрума). Многие письма,
которые мы получаем, даже
длиннее, но в них затрагиваются
самые разные темы. Держитесь
одной темы, и — ВУАЛЯ! — у вас
уже статья, а не письмо! Если

### How to Write to OUTLET

Letters are accepted in almost any form for publication in our OUTLETTERS: BASIC PRINT or DATA statements, handwritten or typed pages, a simple JOTTER program is provided in Issue 2 (Opus #4); mailbox messages via Prestel No. 014703943 but the easiest for us to edit are Tasword 2 files with the right-hand margin set at 32.

Please state if there should be parts of your letter you do not wish published but we always use our discretion anyway. Letters may also be edited for clarity and length... Please ask if you welcome direct correspondence from other OUTLET readers and we will publish your full address.

---

**From: Spiros Gaoutsis, Salisbury**

Dear Ron,

Thank you for the issues of OUTLET 5 & 6 which I received yesterday but also I would like to thank you for your compliment about my English. My wife thinks that my English are teribble, especialy the speling. Anyway, the point of writing this letter is that I can't get enough of OUTLET and so I am enclosing a P/O for Issues 5 & 6. [B carts]

Thank you for publishing my letter and the advert but for the advert I forgot to place the price of £35.00 for both [See OUTBOARD — BC]

In one of ZX COMPUTING issues I read a review of BONABANNER but I would like to know a little bit more about it please if possible.

Ron, here I am afraid I will have to ask you if it is possible to transfer OUTLET issues to tape for storage because I will run out of cartridges soon and the only way for me to get them will be by mail order only. I used to buy my cartridges in BOOTS but they do not sell computer hardware any more. I went this morning for some cartridges but they do not sell 'em any more although they are selling SPECDRUMS for £12.99 a kit.

If you want to tell to other OUTLET readers: Woolworths are selling packs of 5 games: AUF WIEDERSEHEN MONTY, MASK, DEATH WISH 3, JACK THE NIPPER II and THING BOUNCES BACK for £9.99. I am not into games but I got a pack just to have around.

I am sorry for taking so much of your valuable time and before you say it I know I am a pain in the !*#%@'!

Yours sincerely,  
Spiros Gaoutsis

P.S. Next time I go back home to Greece I will send you a post card.

**To: Spiros Gaoutsis from Brian**

"Not into games"! — Cor! Leave it out Spiros! — Bet the games pack is in and out of your cassette player like a ferret in a drain pipe factory.

Information about our BONABANNER program can be found in BONADEMO in this issue on Cartridge B.

We're looking into the problem of cassette back-up for OUTLET but don't hold your breath (Well you can if you want). The problem is finding the time to develop the software. It could take weeks of effort with no guarantee of success. The most positive thing that anyone wanting a tape back-up routine can do is contribute something else to OUTLET — A small program or even a picture. I'm sure readers would be interested in anything created with ARTIST II, ART STUDIO, etc. How about a title page for OUTLET? (If you show the Issue number and month make sure you do it AT LEAST 3 MONTHS AHEAD!).

We need articles. We're not too bothered about spelling and grammar. We can polish that up when we edit it. Next time you are writing about a particular subject in a letter to us just keep going for a few paragraphs. Before you know where you are you'll have half a page (2 or 3 Spectrum screens) on one subject.

Then, if you dry up, come back to it later and add to it. You only need one A4 page or so (4 or 5 Spectrum screens) for a very short article. Many letters we receive are longer than that but they obviously cover different subjects. Stick to one theme and HEY PRESTO! — you've an article not a letter! If you can expand on it so much the better. Ideally it would be in a Tasword 2 file, with the right margin set at 32 but we accept hand-written or printed pages, JOTTER files etc.

You see, the best thing anyone can do to support OUTLET and to raise the quality is to send in something. That frees us to spend more time developing better and more sophisticated software for OUTLET. Don't underestimate the importance of even a single item contributed to OUTLET — it can save us hours of work which can then be applied elsewhere.

— Brian

**From: John White**  
**To: Ron & Brian**

First, to close [what, already?] the subject of my faulty RAM chip I have now replaced it with a 4164 [plus a socket!] and my Spectrum is behaving perfectly. By re-editing my Tasword files I have increased the spare disc space from 75K to 120K, as files are now saved with their proper length instead of at least 204 lines [see my letters in recent OUTLETs]. I am very grateful for all the helpful suggestions I have received. Second, here is my entry for the February JIG!BLOX Competition.

Best wishes from John White.

**From Steve Monk — Ashford**

Dear Ron & Brian

Firstly may I offer some help to Tom Ashmore who in the last issue was inquiring about CATologue's and knowing what files where what and at what addresses they where.

Well maybe he should get a copy of The Spectrum Shadow ROM Disassembly. I have found it very useful to see where you chaps at OUTLET have put your code when I hack into some of your programs to tailor them for my purposes.

I too can endorse Stephen Lamb in saying that there are some good articles in Everyday Electronics magazine.

Since I have had a lot of time off work just lately due to a back injury I have built an analogue to digital converter and also several other micro controlled projects for my Speccy, all with some ideas from this mag and also a good book called Spectrum Interfacing and projects by Graham Bishop.

I hope to control a train layout using my now redundant spectrum+ (due to the purchase of +2) it's well within the means of it. As they say somewhere on telly 'WE HAVE THE TECHNOLOGY' or VORT SPRUNG SPRIKKY DICK or words to that effect. Bye for now: Steve.

**From: Norman Pritchard, Newport**

Dear Ron & Brian,

Am returning February A+B as I have difficulty loading, etc... [Now replaced — BC] ...By what I have managed to see so far, this month's OUTLET looks better than ever so keep up the good work.

One suggestion, if I may be so bold. Some parts of the programs talk about "dumps" and "go to" etc. which are items familiar to all you "Clive Sinclairs" but there are some of us out here who could do with a little explanation sometimes. So come on you two — spare a thought for us "Thickies".

Very best wishes,  
Norman Pritchard.

**To Norman Pritchard From Brian**

Trust you now have the replacement Issue 6 and all is well. Ron is using a new FORMAT routine so we hope that there will be less load failures in future.

I take your point about not assuming that everyone knows the terms that we take for granted. It would be impractical and boring to those who DO know the common terminology to give a detailed explanation every time an expression comes up and, of course, we are getting new readers all the time. **From: Paul Rosenthal, Worcs.**

Dear Ron & Brian,

Thanks for sending Issue No.5 of OUTLET through so quickly and I must say that it's great to find other people who use their Spectrums for things other than games playing.

I personally love anything to do with machine code and getting to grips with writing programs using it, but I'm afraid I have not produced any masterpieces as yet. (The time to attempt it would be nice!!). I like the new twin cartridge format, twice the entertainment I suppose and was quite amused by the serial. Paul Rosenthal

Thanks Paul. Glad you're enjoying "TICKET!". Don't hesitate to send in any program you've done — It doesn't have to be a masterpiece and we can always give it a facelift if needed. I don't know why those system variables are unused. They must have been put in at the early planning stage of the ROM and then not needed. I believe Ron has now replaced the faulty cartridge? Sorry! — we have no plans at the moment to go to another ZXM. We are both utterly stretched during this period. We cannot spare the 2 to 3 days it would need to arrange and attend. Wish we could. — Brian

## From: Ian Vaudrey, London, SW9

Dear Mr. Cavers,

Thank you for the copy of OUTLET #7, received a few days ago. In it I noticed a letter from B. McLellan, in which he asks if anyone knows how to transfer "TRIVIAL PURSUIT" to microdrive. Well, I know how to transfer it to the Discovery and I think that the same method will work for Microdrive.

If you've seen the SDC [SPECTRUM DISCOVERY CLUB, see OUTBOARD. — BC] Newsletter then you may know that, since Issue 3, I've had a regular slot covering tape to disk transfer of games software wthout the use of a "magic button" interface or any utilities. I also answer members' queries on this subject and enclosed is a listing of a program I knocked up in reply to a member's letter... [details]

...I hope this is of some use. Please let me know if you would be interested in this sort of program for inclusion in future issues of OUTLET. I could, of course, supply runnable programs on disk if so.

Finally, is there any charge for the inclusion of an item in OUTBOARD and in what form should the item be submitted?

Best Wishes,

### To: Ian Vaudrey from Brian

Many thanks, Ian. Ron has passed on a copy of your listing to Mr. McLellan. If anyone else would like a copy let us know. We'd be glad of any further help of this sort which is absolutely crucial for anyone without a Multiface-type device. I suppose the wise course is to invite readers to write in with any tape to drive transfer problems and see if you have the answer which we'll include in OUTLET if you supply it on disc (We'll put it on the microdrive and Disciple version too of course!).

No charge for OUTBOARD and any form will do (JOTTER or DATA is easiest for us) — Brian

## From: W. Frank Harris, Hexham

Dear Brian,

After the last seven issues, I still like OUTLET. Mainly, it's the novelty: nothing else comes through my mailbox and talks about commonplace computer-things through my Spectrum and its 3 x MD battery. For my vote, you can drop the competitions, puzzles and games — I use the computer almost wholly for Tasword Three letter-writing (including Open University assignments), home accounting and computational work. For the latter, I'd like better programming skill but, time being short, stick to (long-winded) BASIC.

Utilities to make programs easier to write (rather than fancy lettering programs) would be welcome — e.g. an easy-to-use graphing program for scientific formulae. So would programs, utilities, tips, routines etc. with a practical end-use other than pretty pictures. The exception to prove this rule was your "large letter" program which was very effective when I used the screen as a visual aid in a local talk.

My printer is a Brother HR10 via Kempston E: but your programs seldom work on it — I always have to command COPY: REM/1 before line-feed works — or amend the program. A disconcertingly high percentage of programs fail to load. Could be the fault of my equipment I suppose — I sometimes "lose" my own files — even whole carts with the "MD not present" disagnosis. Is it really not possible to fish out byte-by-byte content from these format-aborted carts?

The letters you publish are often repetitious — a little more ruthlessness is suggested to cut out the banal. Your subscribers' points of import can benefit from conciseness. You may wish to consider presenting two types of letter separately — the "computer" letter for Speccy buffs) and "wider view" letter (e.g. about OUTLET). Letters which wallow on from one subject to the next (like this one) become wearying.

Finally, keep listening to your subscribers — but keep making your own decisions about OUTLET. It's an innovative product — but will need updating and freshening before your subscribers lose interest. Keep it meaty and packed with sound, interesting Sp+MD matter and we'll put up with quite a bit that only the other nut finds interesting. Long may it continue to be a welcome monthly visitor — even when, as is inevitable, the novelty wears off. Good luck.

W. Frank Harris

### To: Frank Harris from Brian

Some good points there, Frank. Sorry about the printer problem but if we put a COPY:REM/1 in our routines it may spoil the print-outs of everyone else who is using the Kempston E. The solution may be to alter the dipswitch setting on your printer. Check your printer manual for dipswitch line feed settings. Meanwhile, can any other Kempston E user say whether they have this problem?

Despite all we do, there seems to be an inevitable percentage of microdrive load failures but don't hesitate to return such cartridges and we'll replace them promptly. As for your own files — It's possible to buy byte editors that can recover some lost files but the process is so difficult, time-consuming and downright dubious that I was thinking of making a competition out of one! However, these byte-editors are of little use on cartridges that merely return "microdrive not present".

I am now cutting letters more and more — mainly because I think the size of OUTLETTERS has reached saturation point relative to the overall size of the magazine — and obviously I will snip away the dross before the substance but I hope we keep this informal "chat" atmosphere going.

A simple, two-dimensional graph program might be feasible. If you can reduce a formula to two coordinates, e.g. time and growth, I think I could produce a program to which one could input data — even over a long period with a SAVE option — that would display the information in graph form, bar or pie chart. In fact with 2 or 3 sets of data superimposed for comparison. If you've a particular application in mind I'd be interested if you could let me have something to work at and I'll see what I can do.

— Brian

## From: John Taylor, Grantham

Dear Ron & Brian,

....One idea you might get someone to work on for you is to do a complete index of all the OUTLET cartridges so far. This would be ideal on say MASTERFILE with a short descripton of each program or routine. As my library of OUTLET grows so managing it becomes more of a necessity....

Bye for now and God Bless,  
John Taylor

Thanks, John. I'm keeping your MISTERMIND strategy to myself for now! Let 'em suffer I say! Ron is working on a back issues file but it will be in issue order. I think you may be right about an index though — I'll put another note in my tray! — Brian.

## From: Jacques Singelee, Brussels

Dear Ron and Brian,

Congratulations on your excellent work and thank you for Issues 5, 6, 7.

Suggestions: It seems you do not have enough room on one disk to put all you want on it. I find that the interest of an issue on disk is that we have screens and programs that we can use later in our own programs. Screens are nearly impossible to transfer by means of a paper issue, programs are long to enter and errors are current. So, in this way is a disk based issue very interesting.

The published letters take certainly half the room on a disk and this valuable room should be occupied with programs and screens! It is also not very [enjoyable] to read text screens! So I suggest you make an issue with letters, info and directions for use, on paper and all the rest on disk with a general menu.

I regret that there is generally no option to print the directions for use of the programs. (I don't find them possibly!) I find the idea of a disk for newcomers very, very, good!

Waiting for next issue as soon as possible! — Jacques

### To: Jacques Singelee from Brian

Mercie bien, Jacques.

We try to include options to dump program instructions where possible. Problems are:

1. With a wide range of interfaces, print routines use up extra memory, especially if used in every program.
2. It becomes very difficult to highlight the text on screen for presentation or emphasis as the colour codes cause problems if you send that same text to the printer.
3. It is often extremely difficult to alter contributed programs once written.
4. Some instructions merely explain and contain no real "data" that you need to refer to again.

You will note that one solution we're using in this issue is to put the instructions into OUTLET separately as a text file with the full print options. Another, as in HANDYWIDE last month, is to have an option to dump a SUMMARY of the instructions. Comment ca va? Tres bien, oui?

OUTLETTERS actually takes up about one sixth of the space of the full OUTLET but the idea of producing half of OUTLET as hard copy does have its attractions and is on our hit-list of options.

— Brian

### From Adrian Stocks, Richmond

Dear Ron & Brian,

OUTLET 6 included my letter that mentioned in passing that an EP44 typewriter of mine had been lost while in for repair at W.H. Smiths'. It's only fair for me now to point out that the matter has been resolved and, thanks to the work put in by Smiths', Messrs. Brother have supplied me with a brand new machine to replace the one they lost. A happy ending! (at last).

Adrian Stocks

Thanks, Adrian. You'll probably be interested in the EP44toT2 program in this issue. — Brian.

## КАК НАПИСАТЬ В OUTLET

Письма принимаются практически в любом виде для публикации в наших OUTLETTERS: операторы PRINT или DATA в Бейсике, рукописные или напечатанные на машинке страницы; простая программа JOTTER есть в Issue 2 (Opus #4); сообщения на почтовый ящик через Prestel No. 014703943, но проще всего нам редактировать файлы Tasword 2 с правым полем, установленным на 32.

**От:** Spiros Gaoutsis, Salisbury  
**Дорогой Ron,**

Спасибо за выпуски OUTLET 5 и 6, которые я получил вчера, а также я хотел бы поблагодарить за комплимент по поводу моего английского. Моя жена считает, что мой английский ужасен, особенно правописанее. Как бы то ни было, цель этого письма — мне всё мало OUTLET, поэтому я прилагаю почтовый перевод за выпуски 5 и 6 [картриджи B].

Спасибо за публикацию моего письма и объявления, но в объявлении я забыл указать цену в £35.00 за оба [см. OUTBOARD — BC].

В одном из номеров ZX COMPUTING я читал обзор BONABANNER, но мне хотелось бы узнать о ней чуть побольше, если возможно.

Ron, боюсь, мне придется спросить вас, можно ли переносить выпуски OUTLET на ленту для хранения, потому что картриджи у меня скоро закончатся, и единственный способ их достать — заказывать по почте. Раньше я покупал картриджи в BOOTS, но они больше не продают компьютерное «железо». Я ходил туда сегодня утром за картриджами, но их больше нет, хотя они продают SPECDRUMS по цене £12.99 за комплект.

Если хотите, передайте другим читателям OUTLET: в Woolworths продают сборники из 5 игр: AUF WIEDERSEHEN MONTY, MASK, DEATH WISH 3, JACK THE NIPPER II и THING BOUNCES BACK за £9.99. Я не особо играю, но взял пачку просто чтобы была.

Извините, что отнял столько вашего драгоценного времени, и прежде чем вы это скажете, я сам знаю, что я заноза в !*#%@'!

P.S. В следующий раз, когда поеду домой в Грецию, я пришлю вам открытку.

**Кому: Spiros Gaoutsis от Brian**

«Не особо играю»! — Ну и ну! Брось, Spiros! — Спорим, сборник игр летает туда-сюда из твоего магнитофона, как хорек по заводу водосточных труб!

Информация о нашей программе BONABANNER находится в BONADEMO в этом номере на картридже B.

Мы изучаем вопрос создания копий OUTLET на кассетах, но не затаивайте дыхание (хотя, если хотите, можете). Проблема в том, чтобы найти время на разработку софта. Это может потребовать недель усилий без всякой гарантии успеха. Самое полезное, что может сделать каждый, кто хочет подпрограмму сброса на ленту, — прислать что-нибудь для OUTLET. Небольшую программу или даже картинку. Уверен, читателям было бы интересно все, что создано в ARTIST II, ART STUDIO и т.д. Как насчет титульного экрана для OUTLET? (Если будете указывать номер выпуска и месяц, убедитесь, что делаете это МИНИМУМ НА 3 МЕСЯЦА ВПЕРЕД!).

Нам нужны статьи. Мы не особо переживаем насчет орфографии и грамматики. Мы можем все причесать при редактуре. В следующий раз, когда будете писать на какую-то конкретную тему в письме нам, просто продолжайте еще пару абзацев. Не успеете оглянуться, как у вас выйдет полстраницы (2 или 3 экрана Спектрума) на одну тему.

Затем, если мысли иссякнут, вернитесь к этому позже и допишите. Для очень короткой статьи нужна всего лишь одна страница A4 (4 или 5 экранов Спектрума). Многие письма, которые мы получаем, даже длиннее, но в них затрагиваются самые разные темы. Держитесь одной темы, и — ВУАЛЯ! — у вас уже статья, а не письмо! Если сможете ее расширить — тем лучше. В идеале это должен быть файл Tasword 2 с правым полем на 32, но мы принимаем и рукописные, и напечатанные страницы, файлы JOTTER и т.д.

Видите ли, лучшее, что каждый может сделать для поддержки OUTLET и повышения его качества, — это что-нибудь прислать. Это освободит нам время для создания более качественного и сложного софта для OUTLET. Не недооценивайте важность даже одного вклада в OUTLET — он может сэкономить нам часы работы, которые затем пойдут на другое.

\- Brian

**От Steve Monk - Ashford**  
**Дорогие Ron & Brian,**
